title: Goal Drift x Single-Turn Benchmarks: Long-Horizon Failures Invisible to Short Evals

original_idea.body:
# Goal Drift x Single-Turn Benchmarks: Long-Horizon Failures Invisible to Short Evals

**Problem:** Failure mode A is agentic goal drift over long horizons (the agent slowly deviates from the intended objective). Failure mode B is single-turn / short-horizon benchmarking. The compound effect: short evals score each step as fine while the cumulative drift produces an unsafe end state the benchmark never observes, hiding a long-horizon threat model labs deprioritize.

**Direction:** Build a lightweight multi-step open-model agent on a toy objective (e.g., 'optimize a metric without harming a constraint'). Measure per-step compliance vs end-of-episode constraint violation across episode lengths. Show that per-step (benchmark-style) scores stay high while cumulative drift grows with horizon.

**Why it matters:** Long-horizon goal drift is a >1-year threat model frontier labs under-test for immediate concerns. A cheap toy harness that demonstrates the per-step-vs-cumulative gap is high counterfactual value and reusable, and argues for horizon-aware eval metrics.

**Relevant context:** Subfield: 'evaluations for agentic/autonomous safety failures (tool misuse, uncontrolled delegation, goal drift)'. METR task suites are open-source. ForesightSafety Bench targets frontier risks others ignore.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain to a recognized long-horizon agentic risk (goal drift), with reusable horizon-aware metric as intermediate deliverable.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Building a multi-step agent harness with per-step vs cumulative scoring needs solid ML/agent fundamentals; borderline for first-project novices.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable (per-step vs end-of-episode drift curve on a toy objective), though agent harness adds some dependencies.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Long-horizon (>1yr) threat labs deprioritize; toy harness needs no internal access and benefits from external work.

low_compute.reasoning: Small open-model agent on toy tasks; single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Goal drift studied; the per-step-vs-cumulative-gap demonstration in a toy harness may be partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Goal drift has prior work but the cumulative-gap toy demonstration angle is partly open.
